name: Sałatka winogronowo-porzeczkowa (grape and currant salad)
summary: A light salad of green lettuce, salty feta-style cheese, grapes and currants, drizzled with vinaigrette.
steps: Wash and dry the lettuce leaves, then cut them into narrow strips.
Cut the cheese into batons.
Halve the grapes and remove the seeds, then rinse and dry the currants.
Combine all the prepared ingredients in a bowl, season lightly with salt, sprinkle with parsley, and drizzle with the vinaigrette.
Toss the salad gently and serve immediately.

name: Pierogi ruskie (potato and cheese dumplings)
summary: Classic Polish pierogi filled with mashed potatoes, farmer's cheese (quark) and onions cooked in butter until translucent, seasoned with freshly ground black pepper.
steps: Peel the potatoes, boil until tender in salted water, drain, and mash into a smooth puree.
Peel and finely dice the onions, then cook until translucent in melted butter.
Combine the mashed potatoes with the cooked onions and crumbled quark, then season with salt, black pepper, and pressed garlic.
Roll out the pierogi dough thinly, cut out rounds with a drinking glass, place a tablespoon of filling on each, fold in half, and pinch the edges together.
Drop the pierogi into salted boiling water and cook until they float to the surface.

name: Żurek śląski (Silesian sour rye soup)
summary: A traditional Silesian sour rye soup made with smoked pork belly and kiełbasa, potatoes, garlic, and a generous amount of marjoram.

ingredients.name: white kiełbasa or other cured meat
sour rye soup concentrate (koncentrat żurku)
ingredients.note: 100–200 ml, depending on thickness and acidity

steps: Dice the pork belly or cut it into strips, place it in a pot with cold water, and bring to a boil.
Add the smoked kiełbasa cut into pieces (and optionally the white kiełbasa or other cured meat), the diced potatoes, and the crushed garlic cloves.
Season the soup with a generous amount of marjoram, and salt and black pepper to taste.
Cook for 8–12 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Pour in 100–200 ml of sour rye soup concentrate (depending on its thickness, acidity, and personal preference).
Simmer over low heat for 3–5 minutes, stirring constantly.

name: Bigos (Polish hunter's stew)
summary: Classic Old Polish hunter's stew made with fresh and fermented cabbage, slow-braised with meats, smoked bacon, Polish sausage, wild forest mushrooms, and prunes.
steps: Finely shred the fresh cabbage and sauerkraut, place in a large pot, add the wild mushrooms, bay leaves, whole black peppercorns, and salt, and braise until tender for 2–3 hours.
Dice the smoked bacon and render the fat in a frying pan.
In the rendered bacon fat, fry the chopped onion, sliced meat, and kiełbasa until browned.
Drain any excess liquid from the stewed cabbage if needed, then add the fried meat, kiełbasa, bacon, and onion to the pot along with the pan drippings.
Add the dried prunes and simmer over low heat for several hours (ideally in stages over 2–3 days), until the bigos turns thick and dark brown.
